intent: Increased sensor_count from 5 to 7 to improve line detection resolution and finer steering control. Increased sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 to enhance sensor sensitivity and robustness, especially in curves. Slightly increased wheel_track from 0.13 to 0.15 to improve turning stability and reduce wheel slip during maneuvers. These changes aim to reduce off-track events and improve progress and completion on development tracks.
rationale: The integrator feedback suggests increasing sensor_count to 7 for better line detection resolution, trying sensor_size 0.016 for improved sensitivity, and slightly increasing wheel_track to 0.15 for better turning stability. The previous geometry had 5 sensors evenly spaced near the front center, sensor_size 0.012, and wheel_track 0.13. The race telemetry shows the robot went off track on both oval and s-bend tracks without line loss events, indicating the controller could detect the line but likely lacked fine steering control and stability in curves. Increasing sensor_count to 7 will provide finer spatial resolution of the line position, helping the controller steer more precisely. Increasing sensor_size to 0.016 will improve sensor sensitivity and robustness to noise, especially in curves where line detection is critical. Increasing wheel_track from 0.13 to 0.15 will enhance turning stability and reduce wheel slip, helping maintain control in turns. The other geometry parameters remain unchanged to preserve the balanced baseline. I expect these changes to improve line detection quality and turning stability, reducing off-track events and improving progress and completion rates. I request measurements of completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, and line_loss_events to evaluate these effects in the next race.
